You draw magic from blood. It is represented by your Sangromancy Dice, which fuel powers you have from this subclass. You have a pool of d8s that you can use on Sanguine Thief features. The number of damage dice in the pool equals the number of damage dice as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue Features table. You can't have more Sangromancy Dice than the number of damage dice shown in the Sneak Attack column for your level, unless you have Sangromancy Dice from a different source.

Blood Magic. You can spend Sangromancy Dice instead of @variantrule[Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice] when you cast Sangromancy spells.

Your pool regains all expended dice when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Level 3: Steal Blood

When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can restore 1 Sangromancy Die.

If you are @condition[Bloodied|XPHB], instead of restoring 1 Sangromancy Die when you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can immediately roll the die and regain a number of @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] equal to the roll's total.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Level 9: Bloody Blades

When you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can spend up to 2 @variantrule[Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice] or Sangromancy Dice to create a number of Daggers equal to the number of dice spent in this way. Each Dagger counts as an Arcane Focus for your Sanguine Thief spells, and you can cast spells with Somatic components even if you wield these weapons in one or both hands.

Additionally, when you score a @variantrule[Critical Hit|XPHB] with this weapon, you can cause the weapon to deal extra damage to the target. The extra damage is a number of d8s equal to the number of @variantrule[Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice] or Sangromancy Dice spent on this feature. The extra damage is Necrotic.

The Daggers lasts until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Level 13: Bloodstitch

As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, you can spend 3 @variantrule[Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice] or Sangromancy Dice to fling a wave of needle-like blood shards. When you do so, each creature of your choice in a 30-foot @variantrule[Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation] originating from you must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking [[/damage 3d8 type=necrotic]] damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. You regain 1 @variantrule[Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Die] or Sangromancy Die (your choice) for each creature reduced to 0 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] by this feature.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB|Short] or @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Level 17: Bloody Exit

When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] and spend 5 @variantrule[Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Dice] or Sangromancy Dice to turn into bloody mist. The attack automatically misses you, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, and you regain your normal form. As part of this @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB], you can make an attack with a Melee weapon immediately after you teleport. On a hit, this attack deals an extra [[/damage 5d8 type=necrotic]] damage to the target.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB|Short] or @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

(Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature)

You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with Ranged weapons.

Foundry Note

This feature includes an Active Effect which adds the bonus to Ranged weapon attack rolls.

(Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature)

While you're wearing Light, Medium, or Heavy armor, you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class.

Foundry Note

This feature includes an Active Effect which provides the Armor Class bonus. Disable it when you are not wearing armor.

(Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature)

When you roll damage for an attack you make with a Melee weapon that you are holding with two hands, you can treat any 1 or 2 on a damage die as a 3. The weapon must have the Two-Handed or Versatile property to gain this benefit.

Foundry Note

This effect is not automated.

(Prerequisite: Fighting Style Feature)

When you make an extra attack as a result of using a weapon that has the Light property, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of that attack if you aren't already adding it to the damage.

Foundry Note

This feature is not automated. You can add your modifier in the Situational Bonus field of the damage roll.

You gain a bonus to Constitution saving throws equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of +1).

In addition, once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack roll while you are transformed using Wrath of the Wild, you regain a number of Hit Points equal to [[/r 1d10]] plus your Wisdom modifier, provided you are @status[Bloodied|XPHB] when you hit.

Your psychic powers have manifested in the ability to cast certain spells. You know the @spell[Mage Hand|XPHB] cantrip. You can cast it without Verbal or Somatic components, and you can make the spectral hand &Reference[condition=Invisible].

In addition, you can cast certain spells by expending Focus Points. You can take a @action[Magic|XPHB] action and expend 1 Focus Point to cast @spell[Detect Evil and Good|XPHB] or @spell[Protection from Evil and Good|XPHB]. You can also take a @action[Magic|XPHB] action and expend 2 Focus Points to cast @spell[Hold Person|XPHB], @spell[Levitate|XPHB], or @spell[Shatter|XPHB]. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells, and you can cast them without Material components.

Prerequisite: Level 10+

Cost: 2 Mutation Points

You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls you make with your Wild Shape form's attacks.

Repeatable. You can gain this Mutation more than once, but no more than three times.
You can now attune to up to six magic items at once.

When you die, a larval parasite bursts from your corpse. You control the parasite. The parasite uses the @creature[Rat|XMM] stat block except it has your @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB]; @variantrule[Hit Point Dice|XPHB]; Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; class features; languages; and feats. It can't cast spells. In addition, it has the following ability:

Burrowing Possession. As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, the parasite can cause a Humanoid within 5 feet of it to make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw (your choice) against your Warlock spell save DC. On a failed save, the parasite burrows into the creature, dealing Piercing damage equal to your Warlock level. While burrowed inside a creature, the parasite can't take any action, @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], or @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB], has @variantrule[Cover|XPHB|Total Cover], and has @variantrule[Immunity|XPHB] to all damage except Psychic damage.

On each of the creature's subsequent turns, it can use its action to make a Constitution saving throw against your Warlock spell save DC. If the creature succeeds, the parasite is ejected from its body and into an unoccupied space of the creature's choice within 5 feet of it. If the parasite is burrowed inside the creature when the creature's turn ends, the creature takes Necrotic damage equal to twice your Warlock level. If this damage reduces the creature to 0 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB], it immediately dies, the parasite disappears, and you take over the body of the Humanoid as if you had been targeted by the @spell[Reincarnate|XPHB] spell and rolled the species the Humanoid had been.

If you are returned to life, such as by the @spell[Revivify|XPHB] spell, your parasite immediately disappears.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Your Wrath of the Sea confers two more benefits while active, as detailed below.

Flight. You gain a @variantrule[Fly Speed|XPHB] equal to your @variantrule[Speed|XPHB].

Resistance. You have @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to Cold, Lightning, and Thunder damage.

Your Adventurer's Atlas improves, gaining the following benefits.

Safe Haven. When a map holder would be reduced to 0 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] but not killed outright, that creature can destroy its map. The creature's @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] instead change to a number equal to twice your Artificer level, and the creature is teleported to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you or another map holder of its choice.

Unerring Path. If you are one of the map holders for your Adventurer's Atlas, you can cast @spell[Find the Path|XPHB] without expending a spell slot, without preparing the spell, and without needing spell components. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Using @item[Tinker's Tools|XPHB] or another type of @item[Artisan's Tools|XPHB] with which you have proficiency, you can take a @action[Magic|XPHB] action to create a @creature[Reanimated Companion|RHW] through the power of necromancy and science. The companion manifests in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. You determine the companion's appearance; your choices don't affect the companion's game statistics.

The companion is @variantrule[Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly] to you and your allies and obeys you. It lasts until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB] or until you take a @action[Magic|XPHB] action to dismiss it early, at which point it harmlessly collapses into a pile of viscera. It immediately drops to 0 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] and dies (triggering its Death Burst trait) if you die.

Once you create a companion, you can't do so again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB] or expend a spell slot to create one. You can have only one companion at a time and can't create one while your companion is present.

The Companion in Combat

In combat, the companion acts during your turn. It can move and take its @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] on its own, but the only action it takes is the @action[Dodge|XPHB] action unless you take a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] to command it to take an action. If you have the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition, the companion acts on its own and isn't limited to the @action[Dodge|XPHB] action.

Prerequisite: Level 10+

Cost: 5 Mutation Points

At the start of each of your turns, you regain @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point] regained).

You've adopted the quick thinking of heroes who have outsmarted their foes. On your turn, you can take one of the following actions as a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB]: @action[Dash|XPHB], @action[Disengage|XPHB], or @action[Hide|XPHB].

The vestige manifests, drawing strength from your pact. It uses the @creature[Vestige Companion|AU] stat block and is a Celestial, Fiend, or Undead (choose when you gain this feature). You determine what the vestige looks like, but regardless of its form, the vestige bears features indicating its supernatural origin. For example, you might decide your vestige is an oversize floating skull etched with sigils, a circle of glowing runes, or a constantly shifting abstract shape. The vestige is @variantrule[Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly] to you and your allies and obeys your commands. It vanishes if you die.

The Vestige in Combat. In combat, the vestige acts during your turn. It can move and use its @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] on its own, but the only action it takes is the @action[Dodge|XPHB] action unless you take a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. You can also sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the @action[Attack|XPHB] action to command the vestige to take the Vestige's Strike action. If you have the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition, the vestige acts on its own and isn't limited to the @action[Dodge|XPHB] action.

Disappearance of the Vestige. When the vestige drops to 0 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB], it disappears. You can spend 1 minute performing a magical ceremony to manifest the vestige again; it reappears with its maximum @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, you can temporarily dismiss the vestige to a pocket dimension. As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action while it is temporarily dismissed, you can cause the vestige to reappear in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of you. Whenever the vestige drops to 0 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] or disappears into the pocket dimension, it leaves behind in its space anything it was wearing or carrying.

Vestige Companion
@creature[Vestige Companion|AU]

Whenever you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can summon the vestige in a new form, which appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. You choose its appearance and whether it is a Celestial, Fiend, or Undead. If the vestige is already manifested from this feature, its form changes to the new one.

You have learned how to channel magical energy through objects. See the Player's Handbook for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Artificer spells, which appear in the Artificer spell list later in the class's description.

Tools Required. You produce your Artificer spells through tools. You can use @item[Thieves' Tools|XPHB], @item[Tinker's Tools|XPHB], or another kind of @item[Artisan's Tools|XPHB] with which you have proficiency as a @variantrule[Spellcasting Focus|XPHB], and you must have one of those focuses in hand when you cast an Artificer spell (meaning the spell has an M component when you cast it).

Cantrips. You know two Artificer cantrips of your choice. @spell[Acid Splash|XPHB] and @spell[Prestidigitation|XPHB] are recommended.

Whenever you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Artificer cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Artificer levels 10 and 14, you learn another Artificer cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Artificer Features table.

Spell Slots. The Artificer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Artificer spells. @spell[Cure Wounds|XPHB] and @spell[Grease|XPHB] are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Artificer levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Artificer Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Artificer spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number on the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 5 Artificer, your list of prepared spells can include six Artificer spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination.

If another Artificer feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Artificer spells for you.

Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Artificer spells for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Artificer spells.
When you take the @action[Dash|XPHB] action, instead of moving, you can teleport yourself or an ally within 60 feet of you to the location of your shade.

Your association with death has become so close that you gain the following benefits.

Death's Lament. When you use Wails from the Grave, you can deal the feature's Necrotic damage to both the first and the second creature.

Draw of Death. When you roll @variantrule[Initiative|XPHB], you gain one soul trinket for your Tokens of the Departed if you have none remaining.

description.value: For 10 minutes, you have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on Dexterity checks and Dexterity saving throws.

Your Transmuter's Stone is more versatile. When you create your Transmuter's Stone, you can choose up to two benefits. You can choose each option other than Resistance only once. If you choose Resistance twice, you must choose different damage types. You can change either or both benefits when you cast a Transmutation spell using a spell slot.

In addition, the following are now among your benefit options for Transmuter's Stone.

Mighty Build. The bearer has @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on Strength saving throws. The bearer also counts as one size larger when determining its carrying capacity.

Tremorsense. The bearer gains &Reference[rule=Tremorsense] with a range of 30 feet.

You are naturally able to resist effects that would alter your mind. You gain Advantage on ability checks and saving throws you make against the Charmed, Dazed, Frightened, or Stunned conditions, as well as against Enchantment and Illusion spells.
Your Superiority Die becomes a [[/r d12]].

You have honed your ability to resist mind-altering powers. You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws. If you already have this proficiency, you instead gain proficiency in Intelligence or Charisma saving throws (your choice).

When a spell you cast with a spell slot restores @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] to a creature, that creature regains additional @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] on the turn you cast the spell. The additional @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] equal 2 plus the spell slot's level.

You customize your armor for subtler undertakings. It has the following features:

  • Lightning Launcher. A gemlike node appears on your armor, from which you can shoot bolts of lightning. The launcher counts as a Simple Ranged weapon with a normal range of 90 feet and a long range of 300 feet, and it deals [[/damage 1d6 type=lightning]] damage on a hit. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with the launcher, you can deal an extra [[/damage 1d6 type=lightning]] damage to that target.

  • Powered Steps. Your @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] increases by 5 feet.

  • Dampening Field. You have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on Dexterity (&Reference[skill=Stealth]) checks. If the armor imposes @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB] on such checks, the @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] and @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB] cancel each other, as normal.

When you reach a sorcerer level specified in the Apocalyptic Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

When you expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration as part of an action, a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], or a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB], you can make one @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB] as part of that action, @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], or @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB].
When you take the @action[Attack|XPHB] action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with a casting of one of your Wizard cantrips that has a casting time of an action.

Cost: 1 Mutation Point

As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you can take the @action[Utilize|XPHB] action.

Your Speed increases by 10 feet.

In addition, whenever an ally enters your Aura of Protection for the first time on a turn or starts their turn there, the ally's @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] increases by 10 feet until the end of their next turn.
You gain proficiency in the &Reference[skill=Insight] and &Reference[skill=Medicine] skills and proficiency with the @item[Herbalism Kit|XPHB].

You always have the @spell[Charm Person|XPHB] and @spell[Mirror Image|XPHB] spells prepared.

In addition, immediately after you cast an Enchantment or Illusion spell using a spell slot, you can cause a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the target has the &Reference[condition=Charmed] or &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition (your choice) for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB]. You can also restore your use of it by expending one use of your Bardic Inspiration (no action required).

You become wholly suffused with the wild's ancient and terrible power, granting you the following benefits.

Ominous Strikes. When you hit a creature that has the &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition with an attack roll, that attack deals extra damage equal to your Wisdom modifier.

Persistent Wrath. If you're reduced to 0 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] but not killed outright while transformed using Wrath of the Wild, you can surge with wild power. Your @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] instead change to a number equal to twice your Ranger level. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB]. You can also expend a level 4+ spell slot (no action required) to restore your use of this feature.

Timeless. You have @variantrule[Immunity|XPHB] to the &Reference[condition=Exhaustion] condition.

Cost: 3 Jinx Points

As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you can spend 3 Jinx Points to put a pox on a creature cursed by your Evil Eye. Whenever the creature is about to make an attack roll or saving throw, you can roll [[/r 1d4]] and subtract the number rolled from the total.

This Misfortune ends when the creature is no longer cursed by your Evil Eye.

While your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1] is active, your primal companion has @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

Taking damage can't break your @status[Concentration|XPHB] on any Ranger spells you cast.

In addition, you can take a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] to change the damage type you chose for the Weave the Elements feature to a different damage type in the list. When you do, you can choose a creature that you can see within 30 feet of yourself. That creature must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or take [[/damage 6d6]] damage of the either damage type (your choice).

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once). You regain all expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

You gain proficiency in the &Reference[skill=Medicine] skill and proficiency with the @item[Herbalism Kit|XPHB] and @item[Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB].

Additionally, you have learned to create magical potions.

Crafting. With 10 minutes of work or when you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB|Short] or @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can prepare magical potions if you have an @item[Herbalism Kit|XPHB] or @item[Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB]. When you do so, you must expend a level 1+ spell slot for each potion you create and choose a spell from your spellbook that targets only one creature. The chosen spell must be of an equal or lower level than the expended spell slot.

Consuming. As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], a creature can drink the potion or administer it to another creature within 5 feet of it. When a creature consumes the potion, it becomes the target of the spell as if you had cast it. If the spell requires @status[Concentration|XPHB], the creature that consumes the potion Concentrates on it.

Unconsumed potions last until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB] or until you use this feature again.

Your long nights of vigilance have left your senses attuned to signs of danger, granting you the following benefits.

Darkvision. You gain &Reference[rule=Darkvision] with a range of 60 feet. If you already have &Reference[rule=Darkvision] when you gain this feature, its range increases by 60 feet.

Keen Senses. You have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on @variantrule[Initiative|XPHB] rolls and Wisdom (&Reference[skill=Perception]) checks.

Warning Shout. When you make an @variantrule[Initiative|XPHB] roll, you can take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] to warn creatures of your choice within 30 feet of yourself that can see or hear you. Each creature can then take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] to have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on its @variantrule[Initiative|XPHB] roll and move up to half its @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] without provoking @action[Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks].

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

You learn Misfortunes that you can inflict on those cursed by your Evil Eye.

Misfortunes. You learn two Misfortunes of your choice, which are detailed under "Misfortunes" below.

You learn an additional Misfortune of your choice when you reach Rogue levels 9, 13, and 17. When you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can replace one Misfortune you know with a different one.

Jinx Points. You have 4 Jinx Points. You gain 2 additional Jinx Points at Rogue level 13. To use a Misfortune option, you must spend the number of Jinx Points that it costs.

You regain all expended Jinx Points when you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB|Short] or @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Saving Throws. If a Misfortune requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 + your Charisma or Intelligence modifier (your choice) + your @variantrule[Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus].

The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB] on attack rolls against targets other than you until the end of your next turn.

When you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can use @item[Woodcarver's Tools|XPHB] to carve special sigils into a @item[Rod|XPHB], @item[Staff|XPHB], @item[Wand|XPHB], or Martial Ranged weapon and thereby turn it into your Arcane Firearm. The sigils disappear from the object if you later carve them on a different item. The sigils otherwise last indefinitely.

You can use your Arcane Firearm as a @variantrule[Spellcasting Focus|XPHB] for your Artificer spells. When you cast an Artificer spell through the firearm, roll [[/damage 1d8]], and you gain a bonus to one of the spell's damage rolls equal to the number rolled.

You've been gifted with the ability to impart a fleeting taste of the unknowable on others. When you take a @action[Magic|XPHB] action to cast a spell using a spell slot that targets one or more creatures, you can force one target of the original spell to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, roll on the Eldritch Effects table, and the target creature suffers that effect for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. This effect ends early if you use this feature again.

You can call forth spirits of the dead to empower you and your allies. When you take a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] to give a creature a Bardic Inspiration die, you can call forth the powers of a random spirit. To determine the spirit you channel, roll the Bardic Inspiration die and refer to the Spirits from Beyond table. The spirit remains channeled until you unleash it or until you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB|Short] or @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Controlled Channeling

As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you can expend a use of your Bardic Inspiration and channel a specific spirit. When you do so, choose the spirit from the Spirits from Beyond table rather than rolling. The chosen spirit's corresponding number must be less than or equal to the highest number on your Bardic Inspiration die; for example, if your Bardic Inspiration die is a [[/r d8]], you can choose to channel any spirit up to (and including) the Shade.

Unleashing a Spirit

As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, you can unleash one of your channeled spirits. Choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself as the spirit's target. The spirit then takes effect; if a spirit's effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals your Bard spell save DC.

You have learned to cast spells. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules as an Arcane Trickster.

Cantrips

You know three cantrips: @spell[Mage Hand|XPHB] and two other cantrips of your choice from the Wizard spell list (see that class's section for its list). @spell[Mind Sliver|XPHB] and @spell[Minor Illusion|XPHB] are recommended.

Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one of your cantrips, except @spell[Mage Hand|XPHB], with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Rogue level 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

Spell Slots

The Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Prepared Spells of 1st+ Level

You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 Wizard spells. @spell[Charm Person|XPHB], @spell[Disguise Self|XPHB], and @spell[Fog Cloud|XPHB] are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 7 Rogue, your list of prepared spells can include five Wizard spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

Changing Your Prepared Spells

Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Wizard spell for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability

Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

Spellcasting Focus

You can use an @item[Arcane Focus|XPHB] as a @variantrule[Spellcasting Focus|XPHB] for your Wizard spells.

Lion. While your Rage is active, any of your enemies within 5 feet of you have @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB] on attack rolls against targets other than you or another Barbarian who has this option active.

Ram. While your Rage is active, you can cause a Large or smaller creature to have the &Reference[condition=Prone] condition when you hit it with a melee attack.

Roll [[/r 1d10]] to determine the spell: on a 1, @spell[Confusion|XPHB]; on a 2, @spell[Fireball|XPHB]; on a 3, @spell[Fog Cloud|XPHB]; on a 4, @spell[Fly|XPHB] (cast on a random creature within 60 feet of you), on a 5, @spell[Grease|XPHB]; on a 6, @spell[Levitate|XPHB] (cast on yourself); on a 7, @spell[Magic Missile|XPHB] (cast as a level 5 spell); on an 8, @spell[Mirror Image|XPHB]; on a 9, @spell[Polymorph|XPHB] (cast on yourself), and if you fail the saving throw, you turn into a Goat (see appendix B); on a 10, @spell[See Invisibility|XPHB].

You can inflict disease upon a creature. When you hit a creature with an attack roll using a weapon or @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to give that creature the &Reference[condition=Poisoned] condition for 1 minute. While &Reference[condition=Poisoned] in this way, the target also has the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition. At the end of each of its turns, the &Reference[condition=Poisoned] target makes a Constitution save, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Cost: 2 Mutation Points

You gain a +1 bonus to @variantrule[Armor Class|XPHB].

Repeatable. You can gain this Mutation more than once, but no more than three times.

When you cast a Necromancy spell that targets only one creature, you can have it target a second creature within range.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB]. You can also restore your use of it by expending one use of your Bardic Inspiration dice (no action required).

Cost: 3 Mutation Points

You gain a @variantrule[Fly Speed|XPHB] of 30 feet. For an additional 2 Mutation Points, your @variantrule[Fly Speed|XPHB] increases to 60 feet.

You have discovered more necromantic insights and inscribed them in your spellbook. While holding your spellbook, you gain the following benefits.

Grave Resilience. When you use Arcane Recovery, your &Reference[condition=Exhaustion] level, if any, decreases by 1.

Overwhelming Necrosis. Damage from your Wizard spells and Wizard features ignores @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to Necrotic damage.

When you use your Action Surge, you can choose allies within a 30-foot @variantrule[Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation] originating from yourself, up to a number of allies equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). Each of those allies can immediately take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] to use one of the following options.

Attack. The ally makes one attack with a weapon or an @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB].

Move. The ally moves up to half its @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] without provoking an @action[Opportunity Attack|XPHB].

Cost: 1 Mutation Point

You gain a @variantrule[Climb Speed|XPHB] equal to your speed. For an additional 1 Mutation Point, you gain a @variantrule[Climb Speed|XPHB] equal to twice your @variantrule[Speed|XPHB].

You can always devise the best course of action for the future. You can spend 10 minutes formulating a Perfect Plan, gaining a number of Perfect Plan dice equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1 die), which are d4s. When you make your plan, it includes yourself and any number of willing creatures who remain within 60 feet of you when you make your plan. Those creatures all become a part of your Perfect Plan.

Whenever a creature within 60 feet of you that is a part of your Perfect Plan makes a d20 Test, if that creature can see or hear you, you can use your Reaction and expend one of your Perfect Plan dice, adding the roll to the result of their d20 Test. You can wait until after the d20 is rolled before deciding to use this feature, but must decide before the DM says whether the roll succeeds or fails.

When a Perfect Plan die is rolled, it is lost, and only one Perfect Plan die may be used at a time. 

Once you have made a Perfect Plan, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest, whereupon all unspent Perfect Plan dice are lost.

When you reach level 5, your maximum number of Perfect Plan dice is instead equal to your Intelligence modifier plus your Proficiency Bonus (minimum of 4 dice).

You loudly proclaim what will come to pass when the world ends. As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, you describe the end of days. When you do so, each creature of your choice in a 30-foot @variantrule[Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation] originating from you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes [[/damage 6d6 type=psychic]] damage and [[/damage 6d6 type=force]] damage and has the &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition for 1 minute. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage only. A &Reference[condition=Frightened] creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition on a successful save. If this damage reduces a creature to 0 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB], the creature can be revived only by a @spell[True Resurrection|XPHB] or a @spell[Wish|XPHB] spell.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB] unless you spend 6 Sorcery Points (no action required) to restore your use of it.

You can cast Illusion spells without providing Verbal components, and if an Illusion spell you cast has a range of 10+ feet, the range increases by 60 feet.

You also know the @spell[Minor Illusion|XPHB] cantrip. If you already know it, you learn a different Wizard cantrip of your choice. The cantrip doesn't count against your number of cantrips known. You can create both a sound and an image with a single casting of @spell[Minor Illusion|XPHB], and you can cast it as a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB].

You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor and @item[Shield|XPHB|Shields].

In addition, you can use a Simple or Martial weapon as a @variantrule[Spellcasting Focus|XPHB] to cast spells from your Bard spell list.

When you hit a creature with an attack roll, you can expend one Superiority Die to attempt to frighten the target. Add the Superiority Die to the attack's damage roll. The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition until the end of your next turn.

You gain @variantrule[telepathy|XPHB] out to 60 feet. When you use this @variantrule[telepathy|XPHB], you can simultaneously contact a number of creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one).

Additionally, you gain proficiency in Intelligence saving throws. If you already have this proficiency, you instead gain saving throw proficiency with one ability in which you lack it.

You have @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to Psychic damage. Moreover, if you start your turn with the &Reference[condition=Charmed] or &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition, you can expend a Psionic Energy Die (no action required) and end every effect on yourself giving you those conditions.

When you spend at least 1 Sorcery Point as part of the @action[Magic|XPHB] action or a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] on your turn, you can unleash one of the following magical effects of your choice. You can do so only once per turn.

A creature can only be affected by one Taunt at a time.

Cost: 2 Mutation Points

Your size increases by one category (from Medium to Large, for example). You can spend an additional 2 Mutation Points to increase your size by two categories instead (from Medium to Huge, for example), gaining the benefits of the spell again.

See the @spell[Enlarge/Reduce|XPHB] spell to determine the benefits gained from this ability.

You have the ability to cast a sliver of your curse onto another temporarily. As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. The chosen creature has @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB] on the next @variantrule[D20 Test|XPHB] it makes before the start of your next turn.

Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB|Short] or @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB] unless you spend 1 Sorcery Point (no action required) to restore your use of it.

You can take a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] to take the @action[Help|XPHB] action or touch a creature and restore a number of @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] equal to a roll of your Martial Arts die plus your Wisdom modifier. You can use this feature as though you were in the shade's space.

After much training, you have mastered the psionic disciplines necessary to defend mortals from planar threats. As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, you can spend 5 Focus Points to cast @spell[Dispel Evil and Good|XPHB], @spell[Hold Monster|XPHB], @spell[Telekinesis|XPHB], or @spell[Wall of Force|XPHB]. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells, and you can cast them without Material components.

You keep your magical power and martial focus in perfect balance, allowing you to convert spell slots into Focus Points, or convert Focus Points into spell slots.

Converting Spell Slots to Focus Points. You can expend a spell slot to regain a number of expended Focus Points equal to the slot's level (no action required).

Recovering Spell Slots. When you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB] or use Uncanny Metabolism, you can transform unexpended Focus Points to recover one expended spell slot. The Recovering Spell Slots table shows the cost of recovering a spell slot of a given level, and it lists the minimum Monk level you must be to recover a slot. You can recover a spell slot no higher than level 4.

As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you can expend a use of your Wild Shape feature to take on a starry form rather than shape-shifting.

While in your starry form, you retain your game statistics, but your body becomes luminous, your joints glimmer like stars, and glowing lines connect them as on a star chart. This form sheds @variantrule[Bright Light|XPHB] in a 10-foot radius and @variantrule[Dim Light|XPHB] for an additional 10 feet. The form lasts for 10 minutes. It ends early if you dismiss it (no action required), have the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition, or use this feature again.

Whenever you assume your starry form, choose which of the following constellations glimmers on your body; your choice gives you certain benefits while in the form.

effects.name: Starry Form
effects.description: Your form sheds Bright Light in a 10-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 10 feet.

description.value: You employ agility in your sharpshooting. When a creature you can see misses you with an attack roll, you can take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] to move up to half your @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] away from the attacker without provoking @action[opportunity attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks]. You can then make a ranged attack roll against the attacker as part of this @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] if the attacker is within the weapon's range.

activation.condition: When a creature you can see that is cursed by your Evil Eye would regain Hit Points

description.value:
Cost: 1 Jinx Point

When a creature you can see that is cursed by your Evil Eye would regain @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB], you can take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] and spend 1 Jinx Point to halve the number of @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] regained. Afterward, the creature can't regain @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] until the start of your next turn.

After you use this Misfortune, the creature is no longer cursed by your Evil Eye.

As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you assess a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, when that creature makes an attack roll against you or another creature within 5 feet of you, you can take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] to impose @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB] on that roll and give @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to that damage.

You gain an innate power to drain life from the living. After you take the Attack or @action[Magic|XPHB] action, you can use a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] to make an @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB]. On a hit, the @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB] deals Necrotic damage equal to [[/r 1d6]] plus your Charisma modifier instead of its normal damage.

When you hit a creature with Drain Life, you can expend a Pact Magic spell slot to deal an extra [[/damage 1d8 type=necrotic]] damage to the target, plus another [[/r 1d8]] per level of the spell slot. When you expend a spell slot in this way, you regain @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] equal to the amount of damage dealt.

If you make an attack roll with your @item[Psychic Blade|XPHB] and miss the target, you can roll one Psionic Energy Die and add the number rolled to the attack roll. If this causes the attack to hit, the die is expended.

activation.condition: Miss an Attack Roll with your Psychic Blades

description.value: You can expend 1 Focus Point to cast the @spell[Darkness|XPHB] spell without spell components. You can see within the spell's area when you cast it with this feature. While the spell persists, you can move its area of @variantrule[Darkness|XPHB] to a space within 60 feet of yourself at the start of each of your turns.

As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, you twist your face into a horrifying mask resembling your Hag patron. It lasts for 1 minute, but it ends early if you dismiss it (no action required) or have the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition. While this effect lasts, you gain the benefits listed below.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Horrifying Gaze. As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], choose one Humanoid that you can see and that can see you within 30 feet of you. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition for 1 minute. The &Reference[condition=Frightened] target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that can see you has @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB] on this save.

Paralyzing Gaze. As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, choose one Humanoid that you can see and that can see you within 30 feet of you that has the &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the &Reference[condition=Paralyzed] condition.

On a successful save, the creature takes Necrotic damage equal to your Warlock level, it is no longer &Reference[condition=Frightened], and it can't be targeted by your Hag's Visage again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Death Gaze. As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, choose one Humanoid that you can see and that can see you within 30 feet of you that has the &Reference[condition=Paralyzed] condition. The creature must make a Wisdom saving throw with @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] against your spell save DC or be reduced to 0 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB].

On a successful save, the creature takes Necrotic damage equal to twice your Warlock level, it is no longer &Reference[condition=Paralyzed], and it can't be targeted by your Hag's Visage again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Your patron's powers have a profound effect on your body and magic, granting you the following benefits.

Arcane Necrosis. Necrotic damage from your attacks, Warlock spells, and Warlock features ignores @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to Necrotic damage. Once per turn when you cast a spell that deals damage, you can change that spell's damage type to Necrotic.

Dreaded Necrosis. When you hit a creature with an attack roll and deal Necrotic damage while using your Form of Dread, you can roll one additional damage die when determining the Necrotic damage the target takes. You can use this benefit only once per turn.

Undead Endurance. You don't gain &Reference[condition=Exhaustion] levels from @hazard[dehydration|XPHB], @hazard[malnutrition|XPHB], or @hazard[suffocation|XPHB]. In addition, you don't need to sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep.

You harbor a wellspring of psionic energy within yourself. It is represented by your Psionic Energy Dice, which fuel certain powers you have from this subclass. The Soulknife Energy Dice table shows the number of these dice you have when you reach certain Rogue levels, and the table shows the die size.

You regain one of your expended Psionic Energy Dice when you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB], and you regain all of them when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

The first time you use this power after each @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you don't expend the Psionic Energy Die. All other times you use the power, you expend the die.

As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you adopt an infernal or celestial countenance for 10 minutes. For the duration, your appearance gains aspects of the power you choose. You gain the following benefits.

Commanding Presence. You have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on Charisma checks.

Improved Spells. When you expend a spell slot to cast a spell from the Arch Daemon or Arch Seraph table, the spell is cast as if you had spent a spell slot of one level higher.

Unearthly Wings. You gain a @variantrule[Fly Speed|XPHB] of 60 feet.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB]. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5+ spell slot (no action required).

Every @object[Eldritch Cannon|EFA] you create is now more destructive. You gain the following benefits.

Detonate. When your cannon takes damage, you can take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] to command the cannon to detonate if you are within 60 feet of it. Doing so destroys the cannon and forces each creature within 20 feet of it to make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC, taking [[/damage 3d10 type=force]] damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

Firepower. The cannon's damage rolls and the number of @variantrule[Temporary Hit Points|XPHB] granted by Protector increase by [[/r 1d8]].

Once you cast the spell using this talent, you can't do so again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Your @subclassFeature[Spellfire Burst|Sorcerer|XPHB|Spellfire|FRHoF|3|FRHoF] improves. Your bloodthirst imbues you with preternatural strength and resilience, allowing you to keep sowing slaughter. As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you gain the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB]. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

Crimson Armor. When a creature within your Aura of Protection becomes @condition[Bloodied|XPHB] by an enemy, you gain 30 @variantrule[Temporary Hit Points|XPHB].

Seeing Red. When a creature hits you with an attack roll, you can take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] to make one melee attack against that creature, using a weapon or an @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB].

Wanton Slaughter. When you hit a creature with a melee attack roll using a weapon or an @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], you can choose any number of creatures within 5 feet of the original target and within your reach. Each chosen creature takes Force damage equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) plus your @variantrule[Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus].

When you deal damage with a cantrip or an attack with a weapon or @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], you can deal an additional [[/damage 1d8 type=fire]] damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier plus your @variantrule[Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus] (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB|Short] or @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

When you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can create a magic stone that lasts until you use this feature again. The stone is a Tiny object, and you can use it as a @variantrule[Spellcasting Focus|XPHB] for your Wizard spells. A creature with the stone in its possession gains proficiency in Constitution saving throws and one of the following benefits, which you choose when you create the stone. You can change the stone's benefit when you cast a Transmutation spell using a spell slot.

Darkvision. The bearer gains &Reference[rule=Darkvision] with a range of 60 feet or increases the range of its &Reference[rule=Darkvision] by 60 feet.

They last there for 1 minute or until you have the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition or die. You and your allies have @variantrule[Cover|XPHB|Half Cover] while in that area, and your allies gain the current @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] of your Nature's Ward while there.

Even when things don't work out, you can always regroup and recuperate. Whenever you spend and roll a Perfect Plan die to add to an ability check. If the check fails, you regain the spent Perfect Plan die.

You can attack twice with a Wild Shape form's attack instead of once whenever you take the @action[Attack|XPHB] action on your turn.

Choose one of the following damage types: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. You and your allies have @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to that damage type while in your Aura of Protection.

At the start of each of your turns, you can change the damage type affected by this feature to one of the other listed options (no action required).

You always have @spell[Counterspell|XPHB] prepared.

Additionally, whenever a target fails the saving throw against a @spell[Counterspell|XPHB] you cast, you regain [[/r 1d4]] Sorcery Points.

You have a near-supernatural awareness of your surroundings, ensuring that you are always one step ahead. You gain the following benefits:

  • You can't be surprised.

  • Once per turn, you can use your Perfect Plan dice to add to your own d20 Tests without using your Reaction or expending the dice rolled.

  • Attack rolls made against you are made with Disadvantage.

Choose two Wizard spells from the Enchantment school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Enchantment school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

You gain proficiency in Constitution saving throws. In addition, when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Constitution saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

Cost: 2 Mutation Points

Once per turn, a creature you hit with a Wild Shape form's attack takes an extra [[/damage 2d6 type=poison]] damage, and you can force a creature you hit with a Wild Shape form's attack to make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the creature is &Reference[condition=Poisoned] for 1 minute. It can repeat the saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the &Reference[condition=Poisoned] condition on a success.

Repeatable. You can gain this Mutation more than once, but no more than three times. For each additional 2 Mutation points, the attack does an additional [[/damage 2d6 type=poison]] damage.

When you take the @action[Attack|XPHB] action, you can expend one use of your Channel Divinity to utter a vow of enmity against a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. You have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on attack rolls against the creature for 1 minute or until you use this feature again.

If the creature drops to 0 @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] before the vow ends, you can transfer the vow to a different creature within 30 feet of yourself (no action required).

Your Rage taps into the life force of the World Tree. You gain the following benefits.

Vitality Surge. When you activate your Rage, you gain a number of @variantrule[Temporary Hit Points|XPHB] equal to your Barbarian level.

Life-Giving Force. At the start of each of your turns while your Rage is active, you can choose another creature within 10 feet of yourself to gain @variantrule[Temporary Hit Points|XPHB]. To determine the number of @variantrule[Temporary Hit Points|XPHB], roll a number of d6s equal to your Rage Damage bonus, and add them together. In addition, whenever you or a creature you can see within 120 feet of you succeeds on a saving throw to avoid or end the &Reference[condition=Charmed] or &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition, you can take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] to force a different creature you can see within 120 feet of yourself to make a Wisdom save against your spell save DC. Enhanced Ruinous Smite. Until the end of your next turn, any creature affected by your Ruinous Smite suffers a @variantrule[Critical Hit|XPHB] on a roll of 19-20 on the [[/r d20]].

World Breaker. You regain your use of your Shake the Earth feature when you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB|Short] or @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Taking damage can't break your @status[Concentration|XPHB] on Conjuration spells.

You magically summon a primal beast, which draws strength from your bond with nature. Choose its stat block: @creature[Beast of the Land|XPHB], @creature[Beast of the Sea|XPHB], or @creature[Beast of the Sky|XPHB]. You also determine the kind of animal it is, choosing a kind appropriate for the stat block. Whatever beast you choose, it bears primal markings indicating its supernatural origin.

The beast is Friendly to you and your allies and obeys your commands. It vanishes if you die.

The Beast in Combat. In combat, the beast acts during your turn. It can move and use its @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] on its own, but the only action it takes is the @action[Dodge|XPHB] action unless you take a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] to command it to take an action in its stat block or some other action. You can also sacrifice one of your attacks when you take the @action[Attack|XPHB] action to command the beast to take the Beast's Strike action. If you have the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition, the beast acts on its own and isn't limited to the @action[Dodge|XPHB] action.

Restoring or Replacing the Beast. If the beast has died within the last hour, you can take a @action[Magic|XPHB] action to touch it and expend a spell slot. The beast returns to life after 1 minute with all its @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] restored.

Whenever you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can summon a different primal beast, which appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you. You choose its stat block and appearance. If you already have a beast from this feature, the old one vanishes when the new one appears.

You then teleport to that space, and the blade vanishes.

Unraveling mysteries under the cover of night has honed your skills. You gain the following benefits.

Expertise. Choose one of your skill proficiencies with which you lack @variantrule[Expertise|XPHB]. You gain @variantrule[Expertise|XPHB] in that skill.

Choose two Wizard spells from the Conjuration school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Conjuration school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

You always have the @spell[Find Steed|XPHB] spell prepared. With this feature, you can cast it without a spell slot or components, and your spellcasting ability for it is Intelligence.

Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so in this way again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you can choose a new form for your primal companion, causing it to transform instantaneously. When you cause your primal companion to transform in this way, its current @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] change to its new @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point] maximum.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB|Short] or @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB]. You can also restore your use of it by expending one use of your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1] (no action required).

When you activate your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1], your countenance distorts and your body swells. Creatures that haven't witnessed your transformation, now or previously, don't recognize you. In addition, while your @classFeature[Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1] is active, you gain the following benefits:

  • You can roll [[/r 1d8]] in place of the normal damage of your @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], and whenever you deal damage with an @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], it can deal your choice of Force damage or its normal damage type.
  • When you hit a creature with an @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], you can push it 10 feet or force the creature to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and your @variantrule[Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus]). On a failed save, the creature has the &Reference[condition=Prone] condition.
  • You count as one size larger when determining the success or failure of a Grapple, and when you make an @variantrule[Unarmed Strike|XPHB], your reach is 5 feet greater than normal.

You have uncovered or stolen secret power from agents of the Arch Daemons and Arch Seraphs. You gain one Eldritch Invocation of your choice.

Prerequisites. If an invocation has a prerequisite, you must meet it to learn that invocation. If an invocation has a Warlock level prerequisite, you use your Wizard level instead. For example, if an invocation requires you to be a level 5+ Warlock, you can select the invocation once you reach Wizard level 5.

Replacing and Gaining Invocations. Whenever you gain a Wizard level, you can replace one of your invocations with another one for which you qualify. You can't replace an invocation if it's a prerequisite for another invocation that you have.

You gain an additional invocation when you reach Wizard levels 6 and 14.

You can't pick the same invocation more than once unless its description says otherwise.

Intelligent Invocations. You can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Charisma modifier for your invocations.

Choose two Wizard spells from the Illusion school, each of which must be no higher than level 2, and add them to your spellbook for free.

In addition, whenever you gain access to a new level of spell slots in this class, you can add one Wizard spell from the Illusion school to your spellbook for free. The chosen spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Your spellbook's necromantic secrets grant you additional powers. You gain the following benefits.

Necrotic Resistance. You have @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to Necrotic damage.

Undead Familiar. The @spell[Find Familiar|XPHB] spell appears in your spellbook. When you cast the spell, you choose one of the normal forms for your familiar or one of the following special forms: @creature[Skeleton|XMM] or @creature[Zombie|XMM] (see appendix B of the Player's Handbook for the familiar's stat block). When you choose one of the normal forms, you can choose Undead as its creature type.

Additionally, when you take the @action[Attack|XPHB] action, you can forgo one of your own attacks to allow your familiar to make one attack of its own with its @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB].

Undead Vitality. When you cast a Necromancy spell using a spell slot, you can choose an Undead creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself to regain a number of @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] equal to the level of the spell slot expended plus your Wizard level.

activation.condition: When you cast a Necromancy spell using a spell slot

description.value:
Your connection to the plane of absolute order allows you to equalize chaotic moments. When a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself is about to roll a [[/r d20]] with @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] or @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB], you can take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] to prevent the roll from being affected by @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] and @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB].

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

activation.condition: When a creature you can see within 60 feet is about to roll d20 with Advantage/Disadvantage

Choose one of the Dead Three: @deity[Bane|Faerûnian|FRHoF], @deity[Bhaal|Faerûnian|FRHoF], or @deity[Myrkul|Faerûnian|FRHoF]. You gain @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to one type of damage and the ability to cast a cantrip, as detailed in the table below; Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this cantrip. When you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can change your choice.

GodDamage ResistanceCantrip

@deity[Bhaal|Faerûnian|FRHoF]Poison@spell[Blade Ward|XPHB]

Immediately after you cast @spell[Divine Smite|XPHB], you can expend one use of your @classFeature[Channel Divinity|Paladin|XPHB|3|XPHB] and invoke one of the following effects.

Your advance in battle is the guiding beacon for your allies. Whenever you take the Help action to assist an attack roll, you may use your Guiding Guile feature as if you made an attack roll against the chosen enemy.

Additionally, you can take the Help action as a Bonus Action, but you must spend a Perfect Plan die to do so.

For 1 hour, you count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity, and when you attack with a Melee weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can replace that property with the @itemMastery[Topple|XPHB] property for that attack.

Your experience surviving harrowing environments allows you to bolster your allies in addition to yourself. As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, choose a number of creatures you can see equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one). Each chosen creature regains @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] equal to [[/r 1d10]] plus your Ranger level and has @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on saving throws to avoid or end the &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition for 1 hour.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].
For 1 hour, you have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on saving throws to avoid or end the &Reference[condition=Charmed] or &Reference[condition=Frightened] condition.

When you use your @classFeature[Flash of Genius|Artificer|EFA|7|EFA], you or a willing creature of your choice that you can see within 30 feet of yourself can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see as part of that same @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB].

You have learned to cast Wizard spells, as well as spells from the Sangromancy school. All Sangromancy spells and cantrips are treated as Wizard spells for the purposes of this subclass.

Cantrips. You know three cantrips from the Wizard spell list and from the list of Sangromancy spells. Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Rogue level 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

Spell Slots. The Sanguine Thief Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 Wizard spells.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Sanguine Thief Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Sanguine Thief Spellcasting table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Wizard spell for which you have spell slots.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use an @item[Arcane Focus|XPHB] as a @variantrule[Spellcasting Focus|XPHB] for your Wizard spells.

As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action, you present your @item[Holy Symbol|XPHB] and expend a use of your Channel Divinity to evoke healing energy that can restore a number of @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] equal to five times your Cleric level. Choose @status[Bloodied|XPHB] creatures within 30 feet of yourself (which can include you), and divide those @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] among them. This feature can restore a creature to no more than half its @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point] maximum.

As a Bonus Action, you present your Holy Symbol and expend a use of Channel Divinity to curse one creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself until the start of your next turn. While cursed, the creature has @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB] on attack rolls and saving throws.

When you or an ally you can see hits the cursed target with an attack roll, you can end the curse early (no action required) to make the attack deal extra Necrotic or Radiant damage (your choice) equal to your Cleric level.

Thanks to your athleticism, you have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on @variantrule[Initiative|XPHB] rolls and Strength (&Reference[skill=Athletics]) checks.

In addition, immediately after you score a @variantrule[Critical Hit|XPHB], you can move up to half your @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] without provoking @action[Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks].
When you roll @variantrule[Initiative|XPHB], you can add your Charisma modifier to the roll.

When you expend a level 2+ spell slot to gain Mutation Points, you regain one expended spell slot. The slot you regain must be of a level lower than the slot you expended and can't be higher than level 5.

In addition, while in Wild Shape form, you gain the following benefits.

Unnatural Attacks. Each of your attacks in Wild Shape form can deal its normal damage type or Force damage. You make this choice each time you hit with those attacks.

Unnerving Aura. You have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on Charisma (&Reference[skill=Deception] or &Reference[skill=Intimidation]) and Wisdom (&Reference[skill=AnimalHandling]{Animal Handling}) checks.

You know the @spell[Mending|XPHB] cantrip.

As a @action[Magic|XPHB] action while holding @item[Tinker's Tools|XPHB], you can create one item in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of yourself, choosing the item from the following list:

See the rules for the item in the Player's Handbook. The item lasts until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], at which point it vanishes.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Your connection to undeath saturates your body. You gain the following benefits.

Necrotic Resilience. You have @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to Necrotic damage. While using your Form of Dread, you have @variantrule[Immunity|XPHB] to Necrotic damage.

Unholy Resuscitation. If you drop to 0 Hit Points and don't die outright, you can cause your body to erupt with deathly energy. Each creature of your choice in a 30-foot @variantrule[Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation] originating from you makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC, taking Necrotic damage equal to [[/r 2d10]] plus your Charisma modifier on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Your Hit Points then change to twice your Warlock level, and you gain 1 &Reference[condition=Exhaustion] level.

Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a @variantrule[Short Rest|XPHB|Short] or @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Your patron has taught you to siphon magic from your enemies and make it your own. Immediately after a creature you can see within 60 feet of you casts a spell, you can take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] to force the creature to make a Charisma saving throw. The DC equals your spell save DC. On a failed save, that creature can't cast a spell again until 8 hours have passed. While this effect lasts, if the spell was at least level 1 and of a level you can cast, you have that spell prepared.

The maximum number of spell levels you can have siphoned at once equals 1 plus your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1). If you have the &Reference[condition=Incapacitated] condition or die, you lose all siphoned spells. When you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you lose all siphoned spells.

Cost: 2 Jinx Points

As a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you can spend 2 Jinx Points to increase the duration of your Evil Eye to 1 hour or until you mark a different creature with your Evil Eye, whichever comes first.

Additionally, while a creature is affected by this curse, you always know the direction and distance to the creature while the two of you are on the same plane of existence.

When you reach an Artificer level specified in the Battle Smith Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

With 1 hour of work or when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB], you can use an @item[Herbalism Kit|XPHB] to mark yourself with elemental patterns. You gain @variantrule[Resistance|XPHB] to one of the following damage types of your choice until you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB]: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder.

When either you hit a target with an attack roll using a magic weapon or your @creature[Steel Defender|EFA] hits a target, you can channel magical energy through the strike to create one of the following effects:

  • Destructive Energy. The target takes an extra [[/damage 2d6 type=force]] damage.

  • Restorative Energy. Choose one creature or object you can see within 30 feet of the target. Healing energy flows into the chosen recipient, restoring [[/r 2d6]] @variantrule[Hit Points|XPHB] to it.

You can use this energy a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), but you can do so no more than once per turn. You regain all expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Your Arcane Armor gains additional benefits based on its model, as detailed below.

Dreadnaught. The damage die of your Force Demolisher increases to [[/damage 2d6 type=force]] damage.

In addition, when you use your Giant Stature, your reach increases by 10 feet, your size can increase to Large or Huge (your choice), and you have @variantrule[Advantage|XPHB] on Strength checks and Strength saving throws for the duration.

Guardian. The damage die of your Thunder Pulse increases to [[/damage 1d10 type=thunder]] damage.

In addition, when a Huge or smaller creature you can see ends its turn within 30 feet of you, you can take a @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] to magically force that creature to make a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you pull the creature up to 25 feet directly toward you to an unoccupied space. If you pull the target to a space within 5 feet of yourself, you can make a melee weapon attack against it as part of this @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB].

You can take this @variantrule[Reaction|XPHB] a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].

Infiltrator. The damage die of your Lightning Launcher increases to [[/damage 2d6 type=lightning]] damage. Any creature that takes Lightning damage from your Lightning Launcher glimmers with magical light until the start of your next turn. The glimmering creature sheds @variantrule[Dim Light|XPHB] in a 5-foot radius, and it has @variantrule[Disadvantage|XPHB] on attack rolls against you, as the light jolts it if it attacks you.

Additionally, as a @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB], you can gain a @variantrule[Fly Speed|XPHB] equal to twice your @variantrule[Speed|XPHB] until the end of the current turn. You can take this @variantrule[Bonus Action|XPHB] a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a @variantrule[Long Rest|XPHB].
